articles.title: The Nice Ones review – invasion of the sunny personality snatchers
articles.summary: Peter Stylianou’s watchably unsettling tale of unbalanced minds and Unidentified Aerial Phenomena does its best to please. Drone shots are two-a-penny in cinema these days, but it’s a mark of this £80,000 British indie sci-fi’s visual astuteness that it largely avoids them in a film plagued by…
body: Kate chews over this anomaly with boyfriend Dale (Emrhys Cooper), en route to a get-together of his old uni gang in a countryside Airbnb. Already not at ease among his mates, Kate gets a ribbing when she repeats her UFO story (or Unidentified Aerial Phenomena, as they are called these days). And there are knowing glances about her psychiatric history: she once fended off an abusive boyfriend at knifepoint, insisting he was possessed. But if she is delusional, then it seems to be spreading: her one ally, spacey teacher Shelly (Ayvianna Snow), re-enters the room after a suspiciously long fag break, marvelling about how they will all imminently join “the light”.

If Stylianou doesn’t excel at the interpersonal nitty-gritty, he has a way with general unsettling ambience. With cinematographer Alexey Korobko shooting in penumbral gloom, lit up by the icy peepers of the hijacked guests, The Nice Ones drums up enough ominous vibes to remain watchable throughout. Led by Snow as the beatifically raving liberator, there are even a few moments when it seems as though Stylianou is in thrall to the pulpy spirit of vintage John Carpenter.
points: Peter Stylianou’s watchably unsettling tale of unbalanced minds and Unidentified Aerial Phenomena does its best to please.

articles.title: The DCU’s James Gunn and Peter Safran are out – this is the biggest disaster to hit superhero movies in years
articles.summary: The adventurous weirdness of the Gunn/Safran era that fans responded to is now history. Can the DCU ever get back on track? What was Warner Bros’ plan in 2022, when the studio decided to reboot its superhero output, jettison the increasingly muddled DC Extended Universe (DCEU) and replace it with a…
body: Fast forward four years, and that plan lies in tatters. Gunn and his fellow DC Studios CEO Peter Safran have this week been fired (though they will reportedly stay on as film-makers), and Jeremy Latcham, another former Marvel man, is the new boss. What is the plan now? Nobody seems to know, and there is not much point asking David Ellison, the man whose Skydance empire has now gobbled up two of the former big five Hollywood studios (Paramount last year and Warner last month). That would be like asking for directions from a man who has just set fire to the map.

We were told that Gunn was going to finally make sense of DC – which had always been Marvel’s poor relation on the big screen – and deliver a shared universe that would take advantage of the comic book publisher’s rich cavalcade of heroes, villains and assorted caped lunatics. Warner Bros Discovery CEO David Zaslav spoke of a “bold 10-year plan” for the superhero studio after the Gunn-directed Superman delivered a strong start for the franchise last summer, with $618m at the global box office and decent reviews.
points: The adventurous weirdness of the Gunn/Safran era that fans responded to is now history.

articles.title: ‘Hunting Alice Bell’ Showrunner Says Simon Pegg Thriller Highlights Dangers of Online Sleuthing: It ‘Can Happen to Anyone’
articles.summary: “Hunting Alice Bell” is a new thriller about the dangers of online sleuthing from an unusual source. Co-created by comedian David Baddiel and The Guardian’s long-time TV critic Peter Bradshaw, it tells the story of five women who find themselves the target of some of the internet’s most toxic…
body: The six-episode show opens with Fran, played by Alexandra Roach (“Lazarus”), an ordinary working mother whose life is turned upside down when she finds her name and face plastered all over social media alongside claims she enabled killer surgeon Jason Nash (Simon Pegg). But Fran soon realizes she’s not the only innocent woman who’s been implicated. “Basically the women band together and they come out fighting as a unit,” Baddiel tells Variety. “And that creates its own reaction because often the internet is reaction and then more reaction to the reaction.”

The show, which premiered last week on Channel 4 in the U.K. (Sphere Abacus are repping global sales) was inspired, in part, by a documentary about Maxine Carr, a British teaching assistant who in 2002 notoriously provided an alibi for her boyfriend, Ian Huntley, before he was convicted of abducting and murdering two young schoolgirls.

articles.title: Grammy Nominations 2027: The Complete List (Updating Live)
articles.summary: Nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards are being announced Monday morning by Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. and celebrity guests. Nominees in all 100 categories are being revealed over the course of a morning livestream that is slated to run for just over an hour, starting at 4:45 a.m.
body: Read here for the complete list of nominees in all 100 categories.

Variety is updating the list of contenders for the 69th annual awards the moment they roll out. As the nominations are being announced, keep refreshing this page to see the latest updates. Then return once the rollout is over to see the complete list, along with analysis of which artists fared best with the most nominations.

This year’s rollout is different than previous years. In the past, the Grammys have first revealed the nominees in about 25 categories in a livestream, then published the full list afterward. This marks the first time that nominations in every category — now up to 100 — will be read out loud as part of the livestream. With the expanded length, it is expected to end a little before 6 a.m. PT/9 PT. Naturally, several of the key categories — album, record and song of the year — will be saved for last in the livestream.

Among those predicted to score nominations this year are Olivia Rodrigo, Olivia Dean, Ella Langley, Rosalia, Taylor Swift, Bruno Mars, Raye, Tame Impala, Ariana Grande, Kacey Musgraves, Sienna Spiro, Geese and Noah Kahan.

articles.title: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?
articles.summary: In 1961, a group of Italian creatives crossed the border to collect anti-Franco resistance songs and share them with the world – sparking intense backlash from the dictator. A new documentary retraces that perilous journey.
body: I n the summer of 1961, four Italians crossed the Pyrenees into fascist Spain. Unknown to the border guards, their car was loaded with microfilm, a tape recorder and, tucked in the pocket of a writer and musician named Sergio Liberovici, a book of matches – each split in half, etched with the addresses of Spanish antifascists in miniature and glued back together, a hairline fracture concealing secrets that, if discovered, could result in jail or worse.

Throughout their month-long journey, Cantacronache collected dozens of antifascist songs from workers, intellectuals, musicians and poets. Some were mournful laments that described the hardships under fascism; others called Franco a bastard. All painted a groundswell of resistance that embarrassed the dictator and caused an international scandal on the publication of a 1962 songbook, Canti della Nuova Resistenza Spagnola (Songs of the New Spanish Resistance).

articles.title: ‘BerleeN_’ Director Ahmad Abdalla on Telling the ‘Extremely Surreal’ Stories of Arab Migrants Living in Berlin and ‘How We Deal With Fear’
articles.summary: For Egyptian filmmaker Ahmad Abdalla, the idea for “BerleeN_” grew out of stories shared by friends and relatives who had left their homes across the Arab world to build new lives in the German capital.
body: Rather than build the film around a single protagonist, Abdalla drew on these encounters to weave together three stories that unfold over one day in Berlin, blending drama, crime and mystery. The characters’ experiences are shaped as much by the lives they left behind as by the city in which they’re building new ones. “Those people behave this way because they are in Berlin,” he explains.

“BerleeN_” marks Abdalla’s return to Cairo Film Festival, where his previous feature, “ 19B,” premiered in the International Competition in 2022. The filmmaker’s credits also include “Microphone” (2010), “ Rags and Tatters ” (2013) and “ EXT/Night ” (2018).
As Abdalla developed the screenplay, he realized that beneath the characters’ different circumstances lay a common thread: fear.

“The main thing I terribly wanted to speak about was fear,” he explains. “How we deal with fear, and how we deal with our existence on a philosophical level.” He points to the rapid changes shaping the world around us as a major source of that emotion.

body: Nicola Coughlan will not be tuning in to HBO ‘s new “ Harry Potter ” series over her disagreement with J.K. Rowling ‘s views on trans rights.

Coughlan clashed with Rowling last year after the author celebrated the U.K. Supreme Court’s ruling that the legal definition of a woman is based on biological sex. Following the decision, Rowling posted a photo of herself on X smoking a cigar with the caption: “I love it when a plan comes together.”

In response, Coughlan reposted an article from The Cut on her Instagram Story with the headline “This Is a New Low for J.K. Rowling,” writing alongside it: “Keep your new ‘Harry Potter’ lads. Wouldn’t touch it with a 10 foot pole.”
Rowling later claimed not to know who Coughlan was, nor “The Mandalorian” star Pedro Pascal, who has similarly criticized her views.

articles.title: ‘I’m a smalltown girl with a terrible disability. He’s a Hollywood superstar. But we’ve been laughing since we met’: Emma Fogarty and Colin Farrell on their extraordinary story
articles.summary: She has a rare debilitating skin condition but still tackled a marathon, helped by her old friend. As new film The Slightest Touch tells the full story of that emotional day, its stars talk about their lifelong bond – and why he opened up about parenthood.
body: Last month, HBO sent a private jet to Dublin to fly the star of a new documentary to London for the premiere. Colin Farrell appears in the film. But the private jet was not for him. The VIP passenger was Emma Fogarty, who has a rare, incurable genetic skin condition, epidermolysis bullosa or EB. Taking a commercial flight would have been physically impossible for her. As a publicist working on the film whispered to me, it was the one time you can emit all that carbon with a clean conscience.

Fogarty was born 42 years ago. When she was diagnosed with EB, her parents were told she was unlikely to survive a week – which was probably for the best, said the doctor. With EB, the proteins that hold the layers of skin together are missing or faulty, leaving it as fragile as a butterfly’s wings. The slightest knock or bang can cause the skin to tear or blister; 80% of Fogarty’s body is without skin, and is wrapped in bandages to protect the wounds.

articles.title: Tourette's film I Swear wins three Scottish Baftas
articles.summary: The film about Tourette syndrome campaigner John Davidson won Best Film, Best Director and Best Actor.
body: I Swear was the big winner at the Bafta Scotland awards on Sunday.
The condition causes involuntary vocal and physical tics and, in Davidson's case, coprolalia, which causes him to shout offensive and inappropriate phrases.

Davidson was at the centre of controversy when he attended the Bafta film awards earlier this year. His shouts, which included a racial slur, were heard in the hall during the event and broadcast in the BBC coverage of the event.
Davidson, from Galashiels, said he had been deeply affected by the experience but was determined to attend the awards in Glasgow, where I Swear was nominated in six categories.

articles.title: Russell Brand's lack of remorse in prison message 'revolting', Miliband says
articles.summary: London Victims' Commissioner Andrea Simon also criticised Brand for message on his podcast saying he was innocent.
body: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has called Russell Brand's message in which he claimed he was not guilty of the offences he's been jailed for as "disgusting" and showing "no remorse".
Brand has been convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault, and is serving a 10-and-half-year sentence. He is currently being held at HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire.
His wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, in which the convicted rapist claimed: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for."

The Victims' Commissioner for London, Andrea Simon, told Radio 4's Today programme that Brand's claims of innocence will "certainly retraumatise his victims and other survivors of rape who have to hear it".

articles.title: Nicola Coughlan “Will Not Be Watching” HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’: “And I Would Never Be in It”
articles.summary: "I know people involved in those shows, and they’re nice people and whatever, but it’s not for me," said the 'Bridgerton' star, who has previously confronted author J.K. Rowling over her transphobia.
body: The Bridgerton star sat down with British outlet The Observer to discuss her latest role in Channel 4’s I Am Helen, the next installment of Dominic Savage’s BAFTA-winning anthology series set to hit U.K. screens on Monday.

She also, Rebecca Nicholson writes, marched for the legalization of abortion in her native Ireland and has consistently championed transgender rights. And last year, Coughlan was caught up in an online feud with Harry Potter author J.K. Rowling when the latter cheered on the U.K. Supreme Court’s ruling on the legal definition of women, which declared it to be based on biological sex. Rowling responded to Coughlan at the time claiming that she did not know who Coughlan was, nor fellow critic Pedro Pascal.
“Me, I could believe,” Coughlan told The Observer. “But Pedro Pascal? You know who Pedro Pascal is, girl. Like, please.”

Coughlan said she “loved” the Harry Potter books when she was younger. “But I will not be watching the new Harry Potter show and I would never be in it,” she added. “Look, I know people that are involved in those shows, and they’re nice people and whatever, but it’s not for me.”
